summary: David N. Lorenzen specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Wesleyan University, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was a professor (1970–2010) and later emeritus professor (2019) at El Colegio de México.

David Nelson worked in Indology and related areas. He held posts at Texas A&M University (attested 1992–1993) and served as the South Asia Bibliographer at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1997–2004).

David Oliver Allen was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied at Amherst College and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary with the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions (1827–1853) and editorial superintendent at the American Mission Press.

David Ownby is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed degrees at Vanderbilt and Harvard, taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993), and served as Professor of History at the Université de Montréal from 1994 to 2023.

David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. His academic career included posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington, where he completed his PhD under David Seyfort Ruegg, he served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.
David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the doctoral supervision of Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

David Peter Lawrence works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 1999–2000) and the University of North Dakota.

David Phillip Stanley works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, later serving as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

David Pingree was an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto E. Neugebauer. He taught at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) before heading the Department of History of Mathematics at Brown University.

David R. Kinsley specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago before serving as department chair at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy is a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the National University of Singapore, where he also taught (1978–1984), before serving at Bunkyo University (1990–2006) and Xavier University (~2007–2010).

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and became a professor at the University of Alberta in 2008.

David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara under Gerald James Larson and Nandini Iyer, and was affiliated with the Asian Humanities Press (attested 2006).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his BA, MA, and Litt.D. at Cambridge. He held fellowships and lectureships at Cambridge (1944–1968), followed by professorships at Michigan and Harvard.
David Ruddell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a sinologist educated at Stanford and Harvard. Since 1996, he has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he has served as dean of Humanities (2012) and professor (2020).

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, he held chairs and professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1993–2000).

David Shea was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (1793–1798) and served as an assistant professor at the East India Company College from 1826 to 1836.

David Slakter works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a master's degree from the University of Liverpool under Christopher Bartley and was appointed assistant professor at Camden County College in 2024.
